patch.value:
## Problem

The memory privacy scanner judges credential values that sit under a credential key inside **JSON** objects, including numeric values. When the text is not valid JSON, for example a single-quoted object such as `{'password': {'value': 123456789}}`, the fallback checks only the immediate value after the key (`{`) and never inspects its descendants. So `remember` admits a numeric credential that the JSON path would refuse, and the pinned SDK's container walk also judges only quoted strings.

This happens on `main` and on pm-memory#51's head. Probe on 2026-11-13: `privacy("{'password': {'value': 123456789}}")` is admitted by both. It was raised in review as PRRT_kwDOVPw2oc626hoD.

## Context

pm-memory#51 adds several bounded fallbacks for non-JSON assignment grammars, and each review round has found another spelling the fallbacks miss. This item covers the **class**: credential descendants in non-JSON containers.

## Expected

- One bounded, linear walker for single-quoted and otherwise non-JSON object and array literals. Every scalar descendant under a credential key, numbers included, goes through the same `credentialLiteral` rules as the JSON path.
- One shared corpus that both the JSON path and the fallback path must refuse, so the two paths cannot drift: nested objects, arrays, numbers, quoted and unquoted keys, escaped quotes.
- Must-allow controls: placeholders and references (`<secret-manager-reference>`, `${X}`), and ordinary prose that mentions the word "password".

## Acceptance

- `{'password': {'value': 123456789}}` and its array and nested variants are refused on both paths, and the shared corpus passes on both.
- The walker stays linear on 100,000-character inputs, so CodeQL reports no polynomial regex.


---

### GitHub comments (2)

> **@unbraind** (2026-11-13T04:51:50Z)
>
> Widening the scope to the whole class: **the non-JSON assignment fallback grammar**. pm-memory#51 fixed these spellings one review round at a time:
> - a literal after a quoted reference suffix;
> - a bracket-wrapped literal after a quoted, closed-quote or unquoted reference;
> - a reference truncated by the scalar matcher;
> - a quadratic rescan of repeated reference assignments;
> - a literal split across short adjacent segments.
> 
> Each round found the next one, which means the fallback needs one grammar and one shared corpus rather than more special cases. Scope for this issue:
> 1. A single bounded tokenizer for assignment values (references, scalars, quoted segments, `<…>` wrappers, annotations), reused by the JSON-adjacent and the fallback paths.
> 2. One corpus that both paths must refuse, including numeric descendants in single-quoted containers (the original report here), plus the must-allow controls (complete references, placeholders, prose).
> 3. A linear-time bound on 500 KB adversarial inputs.
> 
> From now on, a newly reported spelling in this class that `main` also admits is tracked here instead of in #51.

> **@unbraind** (2026-11-13T06:54:43Z)
>
> Another spelling of the class, from pm-memory#51's review at 39c19f0 (PRRT_kwDOVPw2oc62_D0R). In `password="${X}ab""cdefgh"`, the literal that continues *inside* the initial reference quote (`ab`) is not carried into the adjacent run, so `abcdefgh` is never judged as one value. A probe on 2026-11-13 shows that `main` and #51's head both admit it. Add it to the shared corpus; the unified tokenizer handles it once in-quote continuations and adjacent segments are one token stream.
Unify the non-JSON assignment fallback grammar for the privacy scanner (numeric descendants, reference suffix adjacency, split literals)
